entries.title: II Kings 9:1
segments: One of the children of the prophets; a young man who was under the instruction of Elisha and preparing to be a prophet of the Lord.

entries.title: II Kings 9:8
segments: God claims and exercises the right of giving authority to such as he chooses; and all who are intrusted with it are laid under peculiar obligations to employ it according to his will.

entries.title: II Kings 9:10
segments: The portion of Jezreel; the portion of land that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelte,

entries.title: II Kings 9:11
segments:
Ye know the man; that is, to what class of men he belongs. 
 
  His communication; his discourse.  As much as to say, When a prophet comes you expect him to discourse on religious duties.  This was an attempt to evade their question, and they so understood it.

entries.title: II Kings 9:21
segments: The declarations of God in his word are fulfilled in his providence; and though the fulfilment may be long delayed, in due time it will be perfectly accomplished.

entries.title: II Kings 9:22
segments:
Whoredoms; this word is used in the Old Testament to denote idolatry. 
 
  Her witchcrafts--many; expressive of the various superstitious and deceitful practices which Jezebel used to draw the people into idolatry.

entries.title: II Kings 9:25
segments: Laid this burden; denounced this judgment against him and his family.

entries.title: II Kings 9:27
segments: Smite him also in the chariot; Ahazuah at first escaped to Samaria and concealed himself there. But being found, he was brought to Jehu, and by his command slain at the ascent of Gur, by Ibleam.  See

. 
 
Those who associate with the wicked are in danger of partaking in their punishment.

entries.title: II Kings 9:30
segments: Painted her face, and tired her head; intending by her royal attire and demeanor to overawe Jehu.

entries.title: II Kings 9:31
segments: Had Simri peace; as much as to say, You may expect Zimri's fate. See

entries.title: II Kings 9:36
segments: In the portion of Jezreel; Elijah had said, By the wall of Jezreel,
, which was literally fulfilled, since Ahab's palace stood by the wall at the entering of the gate,

.  As Naboth's vineyard was "hard by the palace of Ahab," Jezebel's body may have been taken up and cast into it, as Joram's had been.  Or Jehu may have spoken of her as devoured by the dogs in the portion of Jezreel, because he regarded this as simply a part of the royal establishment. 
 
Men may have a conviction of the truth of divine declarations, and even see their fulfilment in the destruction of the wicked, and yet not forsake their sins, or flee from the wrath to come.
